subject: Private endpoint outbound ownership & proxy configuration (EdgeHealth POC)
messages:
From: EdgeHealth Security <secops@edgehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress & allowlist requirements (POC)

Hi Priya,

We're kicking off the private deployment POC and need to lock down outbound requirements for the control plane and inference traffic leaving our VPC to any Redwood-managed endpoints. Security wants a minimal allowlist and clear ownership: which side (EdgeHealth or Redwood) is responsible for NAT/static egress IPs and TLS/mTLS expectations?

Specifically, can you confirm: 
- A single list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges we can add to our firewall (we want as small a surface as possible)
- Whether your private endpoint package requires mTLS for control-plane API calls, or if TLS with client certs is optional
- Recommended port/protocol list and any DNS names that must resolve outbound (we prefer not to do wide DNS allow rules)
- If Redwood expects outbound to route via our corporate proxy, or if you provide a dedicated static-egress pool for customers that don't want to proxy through the corp perimeter

We're on a tight timeline for the POC next week — would appreciate a technical response we can pass to infra by EOD Wed.

Thanks,
Claire Ng
Security Engineering
EdgeHealth

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: EdgeHealth Security <secops@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress & allowlist requirements (POC)

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. High level first, then we'll follow with a concise artifacts package (attached).

Ownership/Options (summary):
1) Customer-managed proxy (recommended): your infra team terminates outbound egress from your VPC to the internet (corporate proxy/NAT). You add a small set of Redwood destination addresses/FQDNs to the proxy allowlist and optionally permit SNI/TLS only to those hosts. This gives you full control over audit, egress inspection, and DLP.

2) Redwood static egress pool (alternative): for customers who cannot route through a corporate proxy, Redwood can assign a dedicated set of static IPs (NAT addresses) for control-plane and inference outbound traffic. We treat that as an SLA-backed pool and can provide /29 or /28 blocks depending on throughput. Note: this requires contractual commitment and advance provisioning lead time (typically 7-10 business days).

TLS/mTLS: Control-plane APIs use TLS 1.2+ with server certificates by default. mTLS is supported for customers that require mutual authentication for control-plane endpoints — we can enable client cert enforcement per deployment (will need to exchange public certs or integrate with your PKI). For dataplane (inference) connections, we recommend TLS; mTLS is available on request but most customers opt for TLS + token-based auth.

Minimal allowlist (attachments): see attached redwood-private-egress-ip-list.csv. The file contains two sets:
- CORE: addresses required for control-plane callbacks and subscription management (4 IPs)
- OPS_POOL: optional larger pool used for inference egress if you choose Redwood-managed NAT (/29)

Ports/FQDNs:
- TCP 443 outbound to: control.redwood-inference.com, api.redwood-inference.com, metrics.redwood-inference.com
- TCP 443 outbound to any of the CORE IPs listed in the CSV (we prefer FQDN+SNI enforcement where possible)

Next steps we suggest:
- If you want customer proxy mode: provide your proxy allowlist template and we'll map our FQDNs to it (we can also provide SNI fingerprints).
- If you need static egress: confirm desired throughput tier and we will provision a pool and send final CIDRs.

Attachments: redwood-private-egress-ip-list.csv, private-deploy-egress-playbook.pdf (contains runbook for proxy vs static-eip setups).

I've looped in Marcus (Network Eng) and Olga (Security) for the technical details and to confirm mTLS options.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: EdgeHealth Security <secops@edgehealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress & allowlist requirements (POC)

Hi Claire / team — quick technical follow-up with specifics your infra folks requested. Please find the minimal operational constraints below. I've included inline recommendations where we see common customer pitfalls.

1) IP/CIDR details (CORE):
- 34.120.12.16/32 (control callback)
- 34.120.12.17/32 (control API)
- 34.120.12.18/32 (metrics/health)
- 34.120.12.19/32 (auth/token)
(If you choose Redwood-managed NAT for inference, we'll provide an OPS_POOL block similar to 34.120.20.0/29)

2) Port/Protocol:
- Outbound TCP 443 to the addresses above and the FQDNs we listed. No other ports required for normal operation. If you plan to do HTTP inspection, please preserve SNI or allow the FQDNs at the proxy level — we rely on SNI for multi-tenant fronting.

3) TLS / mTLS:
- TLS enforced everywhere. 
- mTLS optional for control-plane: if EdgeHealth requires mTLS, we'll enable per-deployment and provide a CSR workflow. Note that enabling mTLS will require updating your proxy to forward client certs where applicable.

4) DNS and caching notes:
- We recommend allowlisting both the FQDNs and the IPs. If your proxy performs DNS caching aggressively, ensure TTL respect for our domains (typical TTL is 300s).

5) Health-checks and long-lived connections:
- Our inference connections are persistent (keepalives). Ensure your proxy or firewall does not aggressively terminate idle connections below 120s; otherwise you will see additional reconnects and degraded latency.

6) Service account / identity mapping:
- Redwood will provision a service principal for the deployment that will be used for auth. That principal will not perform network-level NAT; you (EdgeHealth) control the egress path when using the proxy.

Action items for us: Marcus will create a one-page network ops checklist you can hand to your infra team. Olga will provide the mTLS enablement checklist if you choose that path.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Ng <cng@edgehealth.com>

Thanks Priya/Marcus — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifying points from our infra lead: 

- We'll proceed with the customer-managed proxy approach (preferred). Please send the one-page network ops checklist you mentioned; that will make handoff easier for our infra team.
- We will not enable mTLS during the initial POC, but we may require it for production. Please include the mTLS enablement checklist so we can scope any proxy changes needed later.
- Can you confirm the expected provisioning lead time if we decide mid-POC to switch to Redwood static egress? We need to plan the procurement window.

If you can get the checklist and the mTLS doc to us by EOD today, infra can implement the allowlist tomorrow morning and we'll validate connectivity on Thursday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Claire Ng
Security Engineering
EdgeHealth
